=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Executive view

The Seller’s package materially departs from the Buyer playbook on nearly every important liability and completion-protection point. The statements that provisions are “standard”, “FINAL”, or agreed at principal level are not evidence of Buyer approval and should be disregarded. In particular, Amelia Frost has not authorised either the 20% general warranty cap or the 18-month claims period.

We should not accept the limitation package or the general disclosure framework as a negotiated whole. A complete SPA mark-up, disclosure bundle and revised completion funds flow are required before approval.

## Material departures and required pushback

### 1. General warranty cap

**Seller position:** 20% of price, or AUD 4.8 million.

**Playbook:** 25%, or AUD 6 million. The 20% position is a fallback available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying the relevant draft. No approval has been given.

**Pushback:** Reinstate the AUD 6 million cap. Do not treat AUD 4.8 million as agreed or use it as a drafting fallback without the required written authority.

The cap must apply only to general Warranty Claims. It must not capture Title/Fundamental Claims, Tax, specific indemnities, payment obligations, covenant claims, fraud or other separately negotiated categories.

---

### 2. De minimis and basket

**Seller position:**

- AUD 25,000 de minimis;
- AUD 250,000 basket; and
- only losses above the basket are recoverable.

**Playbook:**

- AUD 5,000 de minimis;
- AUD 50,000 aggregate basket; and
- once the basket is exceeded, recovery is from the first dollar.

**Pushback:** Replace the Seller thresholds with the playbook thresholds and make the basket tipping rather than deductible.

The Seller proposal is materially worse in three respects: the individual threshold is five times higher, the basket is five times higher, and the basket excludes the first AUD 250,000 of otherwise valid claims. It could also prevent a series of meaningful sub-AUD 25,000 claims from counting at all.

Thresholds should apply only to general Warranty Claims, not Title/Fundamental Claims, Tax claims, specific indemnities, covenant or payment claims, or the fraud-related carve-outs.

---

### 3. General claim period

**Seller position:** 18 months after Completion.

**Playbook:** 24 months. Eighteen months is an approval-only fallback, and no Amelia Frost approval has been given.

**Pushback:** Reinstate 24 months. Any notification provision should require reasonable particulars based on information then available, not impose an unduly technical bar. Timely notification should preserve the claim through its resolution, subject to any expressly negotiated commencement requirement.

---

### 4. Fundamental, Title and capacity claims

**Seller position:** Same cap and time period as general warranties “for administrative simplicity”.

**Playbook:** Separate regime with:

- 100% of the purchase price cap;
- at least six years;
- no general basket or de minimis;
- no Buyer-knowledge bar; and
- appropriate protection for title, ownership, encumbrances, capacity and authority.

**Pushback:** Reject the Seller proposal completely. A defect in ownership or authority strikes at the acquisition of the shares themselves and cannot sensibly be treated as an ordinary operational warranty claim.

Draft an express separate regime and ensure that no general limitation, definitions provision or “all Claims” language overrides it.

---

### 5. Fraud, concealment and deliberate misconduct

**Seller position:** Caps, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to “all Claims of any nature”.

**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all:

- caps;
- thresholds and baskets;
- time limits;
- exclusive-remedy provisions;
- non-reliance provisions; and
- other contractual restrictions,

in each case to the maximum extent enforceable.

**Pushback:** Insert an express, comprehensive carve-out. This is non-waivable under the playbook. It should not be weakened by definitions of “Fraud”, agency restrictions, sole-recourse language, or provisions saying the SPA exhaustively states all remedies.

---

### 6. Overbroad “all Claims” limitation language

The Seller proposes that general limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded, and that exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply across the board.

**Pushback:** Reverse the drafting architecture. General limitations should apply only to expressly identified general Warranty Claims. Maintain separate treatment for:

- Fundamental/Title and capacity claims;
- Tax claims;
- IP claims and indemnities;
- specific indemnities;
- purchase-price and other payment obligations;
- Completion mechanics;
- covenant claims; and
- fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.

This avoids a hidden override caused by a broad definition of “Claim” or an omnibus limitation clause.

---

### 7. General disclosure of the data room and public records

**Seller position:** Every matter contained or referred to in the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records is deemed disclosed.

**Playbook:** Only specific, fair disclosure is acceptable. Whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure must be rejected.

**Pushback:** Delete paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 as general warranty qualifications. Require each exception to:

1. identify the relevant warranty;
2. describe the relevant facts and circumstances with sufficient detail;
3. explain the nature and reasonably apparent scope of the exception; and
4. cross-refer to clearly identified supporting documents.

Mere document dumping, indirect references, or information that a diligent Buyer might piece together should not qualify a warranty. The Seller’s paragraph 1.4 reservation does not remedy inadequate disclosure.

The specific disclosures may identify diligence issues, but their effectiveness as warranty qualifications must be assessed individually against the fair-disclosure standard.

---

### 8. Buyer knowledge

**Seller position:** No claim for anything known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records.

**Playbook:** Delete blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusions.

**Pushback:** Delete the provision. “Discoverable” or constructive knowledge is particularly unacceptable because it converts the entire data room and public record into deemed disclosure.

If any narrow knowledge provision is ultimately considered, it should:

- be limited to actual knowledge of specifically named Buyer individuals;
- exclude advisers’ knowledge and imputed or constructive knowledge;
- not impose a prudent-search obligation; and
- never apply to Title, ownership, encumbrances, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

The playbook’s named-person and reasonable-enquiry formulation relates to Seller knowledge qualifiers, not a broad Buyer-knowledge defence.

---

### 9. Bluefen consent

Bluefen represents approximately AUD 3.6 million of FY26 revenue, said to be about 30%, and the disclosure confirms that neither final consent nor evidence of satisfaction of its conditions has been supplied.

**Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied when written consent is delivered.

**Playbook:** Effective consent and evidence that all associated conditions are satisfied before Completion.

**Pushback:**

- Make receipt of an unconditional, effective consent—or a consent whose conditions have demonstrably been satisfied—a condition precedent.
- Require delivery and Buyer verification of the consent and evidence of compliance with clause 11.3.
- Ensure the consent has not been withdrawn, varied adversely or made subject to an undisclosed waiver, payment, amendment or concession.
- Do not allow Seller reasonable endeavours alone to satisfy the condition.
- Do not allow mere delivery of a conditional document to constitute satisfaction.

Given Bluefen’s revenue concentration, this is a material completion risk rather than a routine deliverable.

---

### 10. Riverlark facility and security releases

The disclosure confirms approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding and no final security discharge has been supplied.

**Seller position:** Release after Completion.

**Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-Completion release requires both an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.

**Pushback:**

- Obtain a current lender-issued payout statement covering principal, accrued interest, fees and break costs.
- Pay Riverlark directly from Completion funds.
- Require releases and discharges of all guarantees and security affecting the Company, shares and assets, effective at or immediately upon Completion.
- Include evidence and filing mechanics for relevant PPSR and other releases.
- Reconcile the payout through the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

Do not accept an unsecured promise that a release will follow Completion. If mechanics genuinely require a post-Completion filing or release, insist on an acceptable irrevocable bank/lender undertaking and obtain Amelia Frost’s written approval before agreeing.

---

### 11. Employee Completion bonuses

The disclosure records AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses, but the funds flow excludes them and does not establish whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.

**Pushback:**

- Quantify the bonuses and every triggered on-cost before Completion.
- Include them as a specific funds-flow line item, or otherwise ensure they are entirely Seller-funded.
- Prevent the liability from remaining in the acquired Company without an equivalent price adjustment, retention or specific indemnity.
- Confirm payment timing, recipients, withholding, payroll tax, superannuation and any leave or termination interactions.

The Seller’s statement that the bonuses are “a matter for the Seller” is not sufficient if the legal or cash liability remains with the Company after Completion.

---

### 12. Ironquay IP

The existing position appears limited to the SOW3 payment, while the documents indicate that transfer of Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment has been supplied.

**Pushback:**

- Obtain a current, independently supported reconciliation or confirmation from Ironquay.
- Require evidence of cleared payment and confirmation that all relevant IP and Project Materials have transferred.
- Preserve an effective pre-Completion cure under SOW3.
- Broaden the indemnity beyond the nominal payment amount to cover losses arising from non-payment, failure of transfer, deficient ownership, infringement exposure, remediation and enforcement.
- Ensure the indemnity is not inadvertently subject to the general cap, basket, knowledge bar or general warranty time limit.

Do not accept AUD 180,000 as either a verified liability or a cap on exposure.

---

### 13. Export/privacy incident

The disclosure appropriately does **not** establish access, exact scope, a confirmed breach, notification duty, harm or loss. We should not overstate the facts in either direction.

**Pushback:**

- Require preservation of access, download, email, system and audit logs.
- Require a properly scoped investigation and continuing written updates through Completion.
- Require preservation of evidence and cooperation with forensic, privacy and export-control advisers.
- Require prompt notice of any access confirmation, scope change, regulator contact, complaint, notification analysis or remediation.
- Obtain a Completion update and appropriate warranty/covenant protection.
- Consider a targeted indemnity or escrow only once the facts and allocation of risk are better developed.

Reject the Seller’s unsupported assertion that the matter is “not expected to be material”, but do not characterise it as a confirmed breach or assign a numeric claim at this stage.

---

### 14. Sandbar renewals

The three renewals total AUD 330,000. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

**Pushback:** Conduct further diligence on:

- executed terms and renewal dates;
- termination and cancellation rights;
- whether services relate to pre- or post-Completion periods;
- accrual and payment status;
- whether commitments were entered into in the ordinary course;
- related-party or linked-contract issues; and
- treatment under working-capital and debt-free/cash-free mechanics.

Do not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct AUD 330,000 from price. Equally, do not accept the Seller’s unsupported “ordinary-course operating costs” characterisation.

---

### 15. Tax and IP are not settled

**Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are settled under the general regime.

**Playbook:** Both remain open, with no assumption of unlimited liability or agreed resolution.

**Pushback:** Expressly reserve Tax and IP. Review their substantive warranties, indemnities, caps, periods, conduct provisions and interaction with disclosure separately. Do not allow silence or the Seller’s update to deem them accepted under the general regime.

---

### 16. Title evidence

**Seller position:** DD-012 share register establishes title to 100% of the shares.

**Playbook:** DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

**Pushback:** Require corroborating evidence addressing:

- valid issue and ownership of all shares;
- fully paid status;
- absence of liens, security interests, options, conversion rights and third-party interests;
- historical transfers and corporate approvals;
- consistency with ASIC records and corporate documents;
- Seller capacity and authority; and
- delivery of valid transfer and Completion documents.

The share register is relevant evidence but cannot replace warranties, Completion deliverables and independent verification.

---

### 17. Office lease and Mossvale

The disclosed documents reportedly identify:

- an office-lease notification obligation, but not landlord consent; and
- a Mossvale assignment restriction, but not a change-of-control consent requirement.

**Recommendation:** Verify the underlying clauses and comply with any notice requirements, but do not assume a consent is required merely because the Seller has disclosed the documents. Nor should these disclosures be drafted broadly enough to qualify unrelated warranties. Confirm whether any ancillary arrangements, novations or operational changes at Completion could independently trigger the provisions.

## Recommended negotiation priorities

### Completion-critical

1. Effective Bluefen consent with evidence that all conditions are satisfied.
2. Current Riverlark payout, direct repayment and effective security releases.
3. Seller-funded and fully quantified employee bonuses and on-costs.
4. Ironquay payment/ownership cure and broader specific indemnity.
5. Updated investigation and evidence-preservation regime for DD-006.
6. Independent title, authority and encumbrance evidence.

### Liability package

1. AUD 6 million general warranty cap.
2. AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 tipping basket.
3. Twenty-four-month general warranty period.
4. Separate 100%/six-year Fundamental and Title regime.
5. Comprehensive fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
6. Limit general limitations to general Warranty Claims only.
7. Reject general data-room/public-record disclosure and blanket Buyer knowledge.

### Reserved/open matters

1. Tax and IP remain open.
2. Investigate Sandbar without assuming Debt treatment or a price deduction.
3. Verify the lease notice and Mossvale provisions without inventing consent requirements.
4. Require a revised SPA, disclosure letter and detailed funds flow; the summary update alone is insufficient for final legal approval.

No approval-only fallback should be conceded or shown as agreed without Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the relevant draft.
